newsitem.title: USA: Tyco offers to buy American Standard - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Tyco offers to buy American Standard - WSJ.

text.p: In a letter dated December 5, 1996, industrial conglomerate Tyco International Ltd proposed buying American Standard Cos for $50 a share in stock and cash, or about $4 billion, plus assumption of debt, The Wall Street Journal reported Monday.
Less than two weeks after it was sent, American Standard disclosed an unusual agreement with with its biggest shareholder, the leveraged buyout firm Kelso & Co, the story said.
Kelso is selling its 27 percent stake in the company, but still would be compensated by American Standard if the company were taken over, the story said.

A Tyco spokesman declined to comment on the letter, obtained by the Journal, other than to confirm its authenticity. The newspaper said it could reach neither American Standard nor Kelso officials for comment Sunday night.

The Journal said it was unclear whether any talks were under way, but the letter indicated this was not the first communication between the two companies. The newspaper said the letter made no threat to proceed with an unsolicited takeover bid.
